title: Dispatch jobs from a stable ref so merges don't disturb running jobs
summary: Today, after a squash merge, Athena rebuilds the local branch (resync_onto_merge) and jobs dispatch from it, so the next job waits. I read this as: cut each job from a pinned commit/ref that a merge never rewrites, so the next job can start while the previous PR is in CI. Each merge must still land exactly one job as one commit. The audience is the maintainer running Athena.

defaults_applied.how: Tests added for the dispatch and landing behavior.
Design doc and decision record updated.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
One focused change to dispatch and landing.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Jobs dispatch from the local branch, which a squash merge forces Athena to rebuild; I did not read the dispatch code in run.rs closely.
Existing stale and merged-unverified protections (P5) stay in force.
No change to governance files is needed.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test shows that after a pull request is squash-merged while a second job is already dispatched, the second job's base and worktree are unchanged and its candidate still lands cleanly. Run cargo test.
A test shows that two jobs dispatched back to back, before the first merges, each land as exactly one commit per merge, with no extra rebuild or merge commits. Run cargo test.
cargo test passes, cargo clippy is clean, and cargo fmt --check passes.

The dispatch source no longer depends on resync_onto_merge having run. The design doc and decisions.md explain the new base rule, the alternatives rejected, and how a job stale against a moved base is handled.
The maintainer can read the docs and see that the next job starts while the earlier pull request is in CI, and that one merge lands one job.

out_of_scope: Automatic merging or re-verification of conflicting jobs
Changing the merge method or the merge_via_rest default
departures: The change touches the dispatch and landing design, so I expect a higher cost and a lower pass rate than the reference.
